_README: THE SPEC LEDGER. Every requirement Ken has given for JobScout, IN HIS OWN WORDS,
with what proves it is live.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-09-22 three releases in a row came back with the same
complaint and nothing reproduced, because the requirements only ever existed in the
chat transcript. Once that scrolled past, the only surviving record was Claude's own
summary - and the summary had recorded the IMPLEMENTATION ('drafts behind Read it /
Redo') as though it were the REQUIREMENT. Ken had asked for 'straight to popup' two
days earlier. Every check after that verified the build against itself, stayed green,
and the product stayed wrong.
THE RULES THIS FILE ENFORCES:
1. `said` is a VERBATIM quote. Never a paraphrase, never Claude's design language.
A paraphrase is how a requirement turns into whatever was built.
2. Every row names the `check` that proves it, or says `none` - and `none` is itself
a finding, not a blank.
3. `status` is one of: live (verified, with evidence), open (not done),
changed (answered differently - NEEDS KEN'S RULING), unverified (believed done,
not proven by a check today).
4. A row is only `live` when something was RUN. Reading the code is `unverified`.
python tools/specs.py            the status table
python tools/specs.py --check    run every named check, fail on any red
python tools/specs.py --new      Ken's messages since the last row that look like
requirements and are not in this file yet
python tools/specs.py --render   rewrite docs/SPECS.md from this file
source: every message Ken sent, pulled from the session transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/C--Workspaces-tbot-platform/*.jsonl, from the redesign brief of 2026-09-18T23:42 onward. Everything before that brief was superseded by it: 'Back to JobScout and we have a new re-design of the entire page.'

Ken: "Each card's bloom to target a different direction from the rest - NW, NE, SE, SW." `bloomer` is back on both card kinds and the motif is pinned to 132px instead of 150% of its host, which is the half that was actually broken - on a card 150% is ~500px of circles crossing the title. A Send it step on both surfaces opens the APPLICATION FORM's own URL - Greenhouse behind its #app anchor, Ashby's /application page - so the posting never opens, puts the whole pack (letter, rebuilt résumé, answered questions, labelled and in order) on the clipboard, and marks the job applied. It stops at Submit and says so on screen: both boards accept an application through their API only with the EMPLOYER's own key, and a browser cannot type into their page from ours. Verified end to end on the web with a real draft (1,107 characters on the clipboard, form URL carried the #app anchor, tracker read 'applied') and on the phone.

specs.said: There seems to be a bug in the rose number on the applications page - it always appears small
specs.evidence: IT WAS REAL, and it was the MOCKUP's. .jcard__score grows from a 44px ring on a card to 52px on the application screens while .jcard__num sat on a fixed --t3, so the bigger ring wore the smaller number; the ratio is now anchored on the card, so cards are untouched and only the ring that grew got a numeral that grew. The SITE was NOT broken: its numeral is SVG text in user units, so the viewBox already scales it (19px of glyph in a 52px ring, 25px in a 64px one) - a first attempt to 'fix' it there put 19.2px on the page, off the type scale, and the sanity suite caught it. Android already derives its numeral from the diameter. check_rose passed throughout because it checks the dots and the band, which were never the broken part.

specs.said: (not reported as such - found while auditing 'everything's squashed up')

The check measures whether two links share a baseline, which is the thing that broke, and measures the target by offsetHeight because the footer is below the fold on its reveal spring and a 44px box reads 42 by rect.

specs.said: There's still no way to save a matched sweep, but I can save individual jobs through the heart
specs.evidence: Nothing is built. A run survives a relaunch on the phone and a reload on the web, but it is ONE run - the current one - and the next run replaces it. The heart saves a posting, not a scoring. Saving a sweep means keeping several scored runs and choosing between them, which is a store and a way to name and pick them, not a flag.

specs.said: I still have the "<-your 8 matches" button on loading the landing page - not sure what those are being scored against if my resume is not persistent anymore

For any and all upgrades, ensure that you strictly stick to the design architecture & language provided by chat. Do not deviate as that just costs us a whole other build!!
